chapters.title: 1. Intro to ES6+ Variables
chapters.content:
JavaScript is a scripting language that enables you to create dynamically updating content. ES6 (ECMAScript 2015) introduced major new features.

Let and Const

const name = "Alice";
let age = 25;

if (age > 18) {
  let isAdult = true;
  console.log(name + " is an adult.");
}
Pro Tip: Default to Const
Always use const by default. Only change it to let if you know the variable's value needs to be reassigned later.

chapters.title: 2. Arrow Functions
chapters.content:
Arrow functions provide a more concise syntax for writing function expressions. They also lexically bind the this value.

Syntax

// Traditional Function
function add(a, b) {
  return a + b;
}

// Arrow Function
const addArrow = (a, b) => a + b;

If the function has only one parameter, you can omit the parentheses around the parameter list.

chapters.title: 3. DOM Manipulation
chapters.content:
The Document Object Model (DOM) connects web pages to scripts. You can use JavaScript to modify the HTML document in real-time.

Selecting Elements

const title = document.querySelector('#main-title');
title.textContent = 'Updated Title';
title.style.color = 'red';

We use querySelector or getElementById to grab elements, then modify their properties.

chapters.title: 4. Fetch API & Async/Await
chapters.content:
The Fetch API provides an interface for fetching resources (including across the network).

Using Async/Await

async function getUser() {
  try {
    const response = await fetch('https://api.example.com/user');
    const data = await response.json();
    console.log(data);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error fetching data:', error);
  }
}
Always Handle Errors
Network requests can fail. Always wrap your await calls in a try/catch block.

chapters.title: 5. Array Methods (map, filter)
chapters.content:
JavaScript arrays have powerful built-in methods for data transformation without mutating the original array.

Map and Filter

const numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];

// Filter even numbers
const evens = numbers.filter(num => num % 2 === 0);

// Map to square values
const squares = numbers.map(num => num * num);

These methods make data processing highly readable and concise!
